To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a single small molecule DPP BDT with NIR I/NIR II fluorescence emission, and excellent photodynamic and thermal performance was developed, and it was successfully used to construct a multifunctional nanotheranostic system for NIR II imaging and photodynamic/phototherapeutic treatment.

we developed a novel small organic molecule DPP BDT with absorption in the 700 nm window and fluorescence emission at 1200 nm, which can be applied as a multifunctional photothermal and photodynamic agent for NIR II fluorescence and photoacoustic imaging guided photodynamic and phototherapeutic combination cancer theranostic.
a novel small molecule phototheranostat was developed, which could be used for the NIR II fluorescence/PAI-guided PDT/PTT combination therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of multifunctional photothermal/photodynamic nanotheranostic based on a single organic molecule, and it will provide new opportunities for the development of theranostics in the future.
the design and construction of a single component small organic molecule-based phototheranostical nanoplatform for simultaneous NIR II imaging and photodynamic/phototheranostics.
the design, synthesis, and biological applications of a small organic molecule photodynamic/phototherapeutic agent for NIR II fluorescence imaging guided photodynamic and phototherapeutic therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study provided a novel strategy of constructing small molecule based multifunctional photothermal/photodynamic nanotheranostic agent for simultaneous fluorescence/photoacoustic multimodal imaging and synergistic phototherapy.
this small molecule-based phototheranostatic platform provides a promising strategy for cancer theranostic applications.
this work has demonstrated the great potentials of DPP BDT as a novel phototheranostically active molecule, which could be used as a promising tool for cancer theranostic applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a single small organic molecule can serve as a versatile nanoplatform for NIR II fluorescence imaging, photoacoustic imaging and phototherapeutic treatment, which is of great significance for the future development of theranostics.

the NIR II fluorescence imaging-guided photodynamic/photothermal combination therapy based on a single-component phototheranostical agent would provide an effective approach to cancer theranostic applications.

a single small organic molecule can be used as a multifunctional phototherapy and phototheranosticity agent, and it is expected that our work would open new perspectives for developing simple small organic molecules with multiple functions in the field of phototheranosttics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the small organic molecule DPP BDT is a promising phototheranostically active agent with great potential in clinical applications.

small molecules with NIR II emission and NIR I absorption can be used to develop novel multifunctional photodynamic and phototherapeutic nanoplatforms for cancer theranostic applications, and the design strategy is of great significance for future theranostic research.

the NIR II fluorescence emission of DPP BDT can be used as an imaging modality to guide photodynamic/phototheranostics to the tumor site, which is a significant advance in the design of phototheranosticals for clinical applications.
